quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: What color are warning signs with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and potential hazards.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help prevent accidents?

options.text: Staying alert.
Spotting hazards and deciding which to address first.
Riding without a headlight.
Keeping space around your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding without a headlight.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, stay alert, spot hazards, and maintain safe distance. Always use your headlight to be visible. Riding without a headlight increases your risk.

questions.question: When riding at night, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Increase your following distance.
Decrease your following distance.
Use your high beam light when possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Decrease your following distance.
questions.explanation: At night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use headlights to see ahead. Use high beams except when following or meeting another vehicle.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: In the part of the lane that lets other drivers see you as soon as possible.
Always in the left lane to stay away from oncoming traffic.
Move slowly up to the intersection.
Weave slightly in your lane so your headlight is more visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the part of the lane that lets other drivers see you as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Position yourself in the lane so other drivers can see you at the earliest moment. For a blind corner to your right, move to the left part of your lane.

questions.question: What should you do when turning on a motorcycle?

options.text: Look close to the front of the motorcycle.
Look ahead through the turn to where you want to go.
Turn your whole body to see through the turn.
Speed up before the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead through the turn to where you want to go.
questions.explanation: Look ahead through the turn toward your destination. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: Why should group riders avoid riding in pairs?

options.text: A merging driver may not see both riders.
Helmet reflections may block riders' vision.
Riders do not have enough space to avoid hazards.
It is too hard for left-side riders to exit a highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders do not have enough space to avoid hazards.
questions.explanation: Riding in pairs does not give riders enough room to maneuver and avoid hazards safely.

questions.question: How can you help a driver safely merge onto the highway from an entrance ramp?

options.text: Stay in your lane; it is not your responsibility.
Change to a different lane away from the ramp if you can.
Move to the shoulder.
Weave within your lane to be more visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change to a different lane away from the ramp if you can.
questions.explanation: Give merging vehicles plenty of space. Move to a different lane if possible. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to create space for the merging driver.

questions.question: What is the best sitting position when riding?

options.text: Your arms hold you up.
You can easily reach the controls.
Your arms are straight when holding the handgrips.
Your knees stay away from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can easily reach the controls.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handgrips. Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.

questions.question: How should a group ride when entering a curve?

options.text: In a single-file formation.
In a staggered formation.
In pairs.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a single-file formation.
questions.explanation: While staggered formation is normally best, groups should switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting highways.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks, what should you do?

options.text: Keep holding the brake; the skid will end.
Release the front brake and do not use it again.
Release the front brake, then quickly squeeze it again.
Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks, release the brake completely right away. Then apply the brake smoothly again.

questions.question: When you are about to pass another vehicle on the left, where should you ride?

options.text: In the right portion of the lane.
In the left portion of the lane.
As close as possible to the vehicle in front of you.
Without signaling, so you don't distract the driver you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When passing another vehicle on the left, ride in the left portion of your lane. Signal before you pass. Check for traffic and only pass when it is safe. Signal again and return to your original lane when you have room.

questions.question: When should you use a larger following distance?

options.text: When roads are slippery.
When it is sunny outside.
When it is colder than usual.
When you are following other motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: When roads are slippery.
questions.explanation: A two-second following distance is normally good enough. Use a larger distance when conditions make it harder to stop, such as wet or icy roads.

questions.question: Long rides in cold weather can cause all of the following, except:

options.text: Fatigue.
Hypothermia.
Severe chills.
Hot flashes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hot flashes.
questions.explanation: Long rides in cold weather can cause severe chills, fatigue, and hypothermia. Wear proper clothing to protect yourself from the cold.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get out of the wobble.
Brake immediately.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
Downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up, as this will make the wobble worse. Instead, grip the handlebars tightly and slowly reduce speed by closing the throttle. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can. Do not use the brakes, as this may make the wobble worse.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: Far from home.
On short trips.
On long rides.
Several hours into the ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles, just a few minutes after the rider starts out.

questions.question: When you make eye contact with another driver:

options.text: It means the driver sees you.
It does not mean the driver will yield to you properly.
It guarantees the driver will yield to you properly.
It may make the driver angry.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean the driver will yield to you properly.
questions.explanation: Never rely on eye contact to know that a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but still do not notice them.

questions.question: To stop quickly on wet pavement, you should:

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Use both brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes if you need to stop quickly on a slippery surface. You can use the front brake on a wet surface if you apply it slowly to prevent the wheel from locking.

questions.question: When a driver makes eye contact with you:

options.text: It means they see you.
It will never happen.
It does not mean they will yield to you properly.
It guarantees they will yield to you properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean they will yield to you properly.
questions.explanation: Never assume that eye contact means a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but do not actually notice them.

questions.question: To help drivers merge onto the highway from an entrance ramp, you should:

options.text: Stay in your lane.
Move to the next lane if you can.
Not worry about it since they are merging, not you.
Ride on the far left shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the next lane if you can.
questions.explanation: Drivers merging onto the highway may not see your motorcycle. Give them space to merge safely by moving to a different lane if possible.

questions.question: A motorcycle horn:

options.text: Is useless.
Usually cannot be heard by others.
Can get someone's attention quickly.
Should not be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can get someone's attention quickly.
questions.explanation: Your horn can help you get someone's attention fast. However, motorcycle horns are quieter than car horns, so other drivers may not hear it. Never rely only on your horn to avoid a hazard.

questions.question: Who must wear a helmet while riding a motorcycle in Colorado?

options.text: All riders
Riders under 18 years old
Riders who have had their license for less than two years
No riders are required to wear helmets

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders under 18 years old
questions.explanation: In Colorado, all riders and passengers under 18 must wear an approved helmet. All motorcycle riders should wear helmets.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift lever on a motorcycle?

options.text: In front of the left footrest
In front of the right footrest
On the left handlebar
On the right handlebar

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: How should you lean a motorcycle when turning?

options.text: Always press the left handlebar
Always press the right handlebar
Press the handlebar opposite the direction of the turn
Press the handlebar in the direction of the turn

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handlebar in the direction of the turn
questions.explanation: To turn, a motorcycle must lean. Press the handlebar in the direction you want to turn to make the motorcycle lean.

questions.question: What formation keeps a group of riders closest together?

options.text: Pyramid
Staggered
Single-file
Compressed

questions.correctAnswerText: Staggered
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps riders close together while giving each rider enough space. Use single-file formation when turning, taking curves, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle on the left, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: The left side of the lane
The center of the lane
The right side of the lane
Either the right or center of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The left side of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of your lane when preparing to pass. This position gives you the best view of the passing lane ahead.
